questions.q: Which of these is a field controlled by a category book record?
options: The employee assigned to the asset
Depreciation method and life in months
The customer invoice number
The vendor's payment terms
questions.explain: A category book record sets the depreciation method, life in months, prorate convention, salvage percentage, and default GL accounts.

questions.q: Why is useful life stored internally in months rather than only in whole years?
options: For precision below whole years, such as a 5-year life stored as 60 months
Because Oracle Fusion Assets cannot process whole-year lives
Because tax books require weekly precision
Because months are required for property tax filings only
questions.explain: Storing life in months allows for precision in lives that aren't a clean number of years, as well as in prorate calculations.

questions.q: Can a category default be overridden on an individual asset?
options: No, category defaults are always final once set
Yes, if there is a genuine reason that specific asset needs different treatment
Only for assets added through mass additions
Only for tax books, never corporate books
questions.explain: Defaults speed up the common case, but a user adding an asset manually can typically override the life, method, or accounts for that specific asset when justified.

questions.q: Why can the same category have two different category book records?
options: Because category books are configured per book, not globally, so corporate and tax books each get their own record
Because every category must be duplicated for audit purposes
Because Oracle Fusion requires two records for every category regardless of books
Because one record is for assets and one is for liabilities
questions.explain: Since category books are configured per asset book, the same category can carry different depreciation rules in a corporate book versus a tax book.

questions.q: What is the risk of an overly coarse category structure when setting up category defaults?
options: It prevents assets from ever being retired
It forces constant manual overrides, defeating the purpose of having defaults
It automatically triggers an impairment review
It disables the mass additions process entirely
questions.explain: If a category groups together assets that genuinely need different depreciation treatment, users end up overriding defaults constantly, undermining the efficiency defaults are meant to provide.
